shared_text:
The flight. An airliner arriving at night at an airport with a short runway, whose landing threshold was displaced along the runway. The report does not give the weather.

The crew. The captain was the pilot flying and the first officer the pilot monitoring.

What happened. During the arrival briefing the captain insisted on landing with flaps 3 rather than full flap. The first officer asked about the landing distance and calculated it: with flaps 3 it was about 300 ft more than with full flap, and it seemed adequate. The first officer reasoned that the runway was 300 to 400 ft longer than the runway at another airport, so it should work out. The crew planned and flew an RNAV approach. In the last 100 ft the flight path became flat and low. The first officer told the captain that they could not land on the displaced threshold. At about 30 to 50 ft the captain pitched the aircraft for the runway threshold, and the crew continued to land.
safe_outcome: The aircraft landed. The first officer thought it had touched down on the usable runway but was not certain; it may have touched down on the displaced threshold. There was no conflict with other traffic. No one was hurt and the aircraft was not damaged.
bad_outcome: The aircraft could not be stopped on the remaining runway. It left the end of the runway at about 30 knots and came to rest on the grass. The passengers were evacuated, and two received minor injuries during the evacuation. The aircraft was slightly damaged.
notes: Rule 3 removed: "for some unknown reason" (about the captain's choice of flaps 3). Rule 5 moved to the safe ending: whether the aircraft touched down on the displaced threshold or the usable runway, which the first officer could not say for certain (the synopsis says "possible touch down in the displaced threshold area"). Kept as reasoning at the time: the first officer's landing-distance check and the comparison with another airport's runway (named in the report; not named here). Judgement calls: "insisted" is kept because it is the reporter's account of what happened in the briefing, not a later characterisation; the report gives no aircraft type, so the class is "an airliner"; no weather is given and "at night" is from the 0001-0600 time block. For James: the sentence "He mentioned that as an FO, other capts would say no" was left out because it is unclear both what it means (say no to what?) and whether it was said at the time. If it means the captain had been refused flaps 3 by other captains as a first officer and said so in the briefing, it belongs in the shared text.
